thread.title: Apple Selloff Offers A Broadcom Opportunity - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO)

author: Shareholders Unite
title: Apple Selloff Offers A Broadcom Opportunity - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO)
text:
Broadcom ( AVGO ) dazzles with its operating margin, free cash flow, coming operational improvements from the CA acquisition and a dividend yield exceeding 4% this year. The shares are actually very reasonably valued.
Texas Instruments ( TXN ) has been a sort of benchmark for us for what a profitable technology hardware company looks, we're referencing the following stylized characteristics:
Steady revenue growth. An amalgam of related niche products in which the company has a dominant position (we have called this a collection of 'German Mittelstand' companies). Enormous free cash flow production, much of it used for dividends and buybacks. We earlier compared companies like Skyworks ( SWKS ) and Analog Devices ( ADI ) as somewhat comparable to Texas Instruments, Broadcom ( AVGO ) roughly seems to fall in the same category.
The picture is somewhat muddied by two acquisitions that have moved the company into new fields with seemingly little relations to semiconductors.
The latest of these was the acquisition of CA Technologies for $18.9B in cash and it closed last November. Last year the company acquired Brocade for $5.5B closed November 2017 :
Singapore-based Broadcom, formerly Avago Technologies, is trying to become the dominant chip supplier. It is known for its connectivity chips used in products ranging from mobiles to servers. California-based Brocade makes networking switches, software and storage products. With this deal, Broadcom will grab more data center products market share by using Brocade’s fiber channel switches that speed up data transfer between servers and storage devices. It will also help the chipmaker dig deeper into the connected devices and cars market.
While partly complementary, the Brocade acquisition also risks losing some focus as networking switches, and especially software and storage products are quite different from connectivity chips.
The CA acquisition is much larger and seemingly less aligned with Broadcom's core capabilities as CA supplies mainframe and enterprise software solutions for very big companies.
However, with a little fantasy one could argue that the company is now more than ever a collection of German Mittelstand companies and there is some relation between the two acquired companies (Q4CC):
SAN switching, which is attaching to storage arrays is very, very connected to mainframes as well in hardware and software the way storage is done
Basically they serve companies who, for whatever reason (regulation, security concerns, etc.) can't make the changeover to the cloud which so many other companies are making, building a private cloud instead (or using a hybrid cloud model), so there are synergies in the go-to market approach.
However, the value of the CA acquisition lies in the change in strategy that is being implemented at CA which looks set to bring big advantages to the bottom line, involving:
Shifting focus to existing customers, rather than acquiring new ones, as the company already has the largest companies as clients. This move will reduce the S&M line considerably. Moving away from perpetual (up-front) licenses to a fully ratable model. And management has great expectations about the inherent profitability of the new business model (Q4CC):
We expect this transition though to take a couple of years given the timing of contract renewals. But once completed, we expect revenues to stabilize at over $3.5 billion annually and grow from there. And to support that revenue base, we do not expect to spend more than $900 million per year. And as a result, we expect to achieve more than $2.5 billion per year in operating profitability from the CA business once we go through this transition.
CA did have a cost basis of $2.4B-$2.5B a year so bringing this down to just $900M is quite a step down. It starts with divesting its $150M a year Veracode business and its service business be increasingly outsourced during the year. Concentrating on its existing customers, rather than new ones will be the biggest part.
The transition is supposed to last 2-3 years while this year's revenue from CA will be $5B. SA contributor Khaveen Jeyaratnam has done a fine job going through the possible effects of the acquisition and restructuring, we give you his conclusion.
While 2019 results dip as a result of restructuring cost and a big increase in a front-loaded share based compensation program, subsequent years (Jeyaratnam):
This is enough to make the deal highly accretive as the present value of cash flows produces a higher intrinsic value for the company when compared to the cash flows without CA. Although, the lower discount rate and higher terminal value contributed to the rise in valuation, it was mostly due to the rise in cash flows. As a result the share price target is higher by 13%.
The company rightly moves away from a quarterly to a yearly focus. The quarterly focus simply contained too much noise and lumpiness (like broadband, the carriers and the cloud companies) through which it was hard to see the significant trends that is shaping up the business.
There are the following sectors before the acquisition of CA:
Wired (41% of revenue in Q4 2018 and growing 1% in 2018), over two-thirds of this is networking and computing offload, with much of the rest in broadband. Enterprise storage (23% of revenue, growing 12%). Wireless (31% of revenue, growing 20% in 2018). Industrial (5% of revenue, growing 12% in 2018). There is a nice overview in the 10-K :
Going forward the company will report in just two sectors:
Infrastructure software business from CA (and some part from Brocade, it's SAN business). Semiconductor solutions. 2018 results Well, growth has been pretty stellar, but much of this comes from acquisitions (the latest one, CA isn't even included here) although the EBITDA growth is really spectacular:
AVGO Revenue (NYSE: TTM ) data by YCharts
And here is another look at it from the 10-K:
You immediately see that the GAAP earnings are hugely inflated by a $12.6B tax benefit as a result of the 2017 Tax Reform Act, the Redomiciliation Transaction and income from continuing operations. The company moved its headquarters from Singapore back to the US.
Q4 results were very good, with an earnings beat of nearly 5% and revenue growing over 12% (still ex-CA).
Guidance The company has 18 week backlog, which is more than a quarter (14 weeks) so there is no immediate threat from a softening world economy but the stock is hardly immune (as we are witnessing at the moment, selling off on soft news out of Apple ( AAPL )).
One advantage of being a sort of collection of German Mittelstand companies is the diversification (Q4CC):
we across so many different end markets, niche markets some of them we do see some of them, your question is, are they all consistently trending down? No, we do not see that, but we do see some that are down and we do see some that are up.
The cloud/hyperscale companies are sustaining the high growth displayed in 2018 according to management, but it warned at the same time for quarterly lumpiness.
Their networking, compute offload business also had a good 2018 even without new product launches, and there will be two new ones driving revenue growth in 2019 (the Tomahawk 3 and the Jericho 2).
The company also intents to regain share in the RF business this year, and expects the broadband market to recover with storage flat and handset and wireless seasonally down in the beginning of the year but will revive in the second half (propelled by the advent of 5G).
2019 non-GAAP guidance :
Revenue will be $24.5B, $19.5B from semiconductor solutions and $5B from infrastructure software ( CA ) Operating margins expected to be 51%. These will be closer to 55% in 2020 when the CA integration nears completion. Net interest expense $1.25B on a total amount of debt of $37B. Depreciation roughly $600M. CapEx roughly $550M. Free cash flow roughly $10B. Stock based compensation roughly $2.1B. Guidance is clouded by some issues:
The change in business model at CA. The change in accounting standard (from 605 to 606). The cutting out of revenue from Veracode, HCI, and (gradually over the year) from the CA service business See also what we have to say about risk below.
Margins AVGO Gross Profit Margin (Quarterly) data by YCharts
The company enjoys very large margins, especially the operating margin is huge; non-GAAP operating margin was a whopping 52.5% in Q4 and further expansion is on the way with the change in the Brocade business model. Management's target for 2020 is 55% operating margin, which really is quite something.
There is of course a large gap between GAAP and non-GAAP figures with substantial share based compensation and acquisition accounting the main sources of the wedge.
Cash AVGO Cash from Operations ( TTM ) data by YCharts
The above figure is extraordinary. The company achieved $8.245B of free cash flow on revenues of $20.85B, that's a 40%+ free cash flow ratio.
AVGO Stock Based Compensation ( TTM ) data by YCharts
Share based compensation is going to jump quite significantly to $2.1B but this is a front-loaded 4 year program and share based compensation will gradually decrease until it reaches their existing levels in 2022.
Apart from acquisitions, here is what the amazing rise in cash flow is also producing:
AVGO Dividends Paid ( TTM ) data by YCharts
And the dividend is going to increase substantially (51%) again to $10.60 in 2019, giving a yield of 4.3% and paying out over $4B in dividends in 2019.
You see that buybacks are a recent phenomenon, but here to management isn't holding back and it's planning for a whopping $8B of buybacks in 2019, even more than the $7.258B last year. That is, the company is returning all free cash flow to shareholders and also the excess cash over their $4B target.
This is somewhat amazing, given the following:
AVGO Net Debt Issuance ( TTM ) data by YCharts
The company is certainly not anywhere near overleveraged, but nevertheless we're a little surprised they're not retiring any debt this year, splashing all free cash flow (and then some) out to shareholders. We think they should retire at least some of the debt.
Valuation AVGO PE Ratio ( TTM ) data by YCharts
Analyst expect an EPS of $22.97 this year, giving the shares a multiple slightly over 10. That's normal for a chips company, but rather cheap for a company with this kind of free cash flow and dividend yield, with the prospect of significant operational improvements to come after digesting the CA acquisition.
As roughly 20% of revenues will be coming from recurring software sales, the multiple on that is also usually much higher and 20% is large enough to lift the multiple on Broadcom as a whole.
The shares have sold off quite substantially in the wake of Apple guiding lower. While this might not be done entirely, we think an opportunity is opening op to establish a starting position if you can bear the risks.
Risk While many of the markets the company serves are experiencing secular growth, there is the distinct risk that slowing economic growth and/or an exploding trade war with China will affect its more cyclical parts. From the 10-K
Keep in mind the accompanying explanation though (10-K):
Net revenue is based on the geographic location of the distributors, OEMs or contract manufacturers who purchased our products, which may differ from the geographic location of the end customers.
That is, US sales are really likely to be more than the 10% suggested in the table. Nevertheless, a stronger dollar is a distinct risk for the company.
You might also notice that the shares have traded as low as $200 this year and have been range bound for over a year ($200-$270). A break-out higher under the present market conditions doesn't seem very likely.
Then there is this, from the 10-K:
We believe aggregate sales to Apple Inc., through all channels, accounted for approximately 25% and more than 20% of our net revenue for fiscal years 2018 and 2017, respectively.
That is of course playing out at the moment, with Apple guiding lower.
Conclusion We think the shares are really quite reasonably priced, both on most multiples apart from the sales multiple, but that's the result of its 50%+ operating margin. We think multiples like this are warranted for the old Broadcom, a semiconductor company, but now part of it is becoming a software company producing recurring revenues
While that part is not big (20%), it should command a much higher multiple and as such should increase the valuation for the company as a whole.
However, the company faces some risk, like a slowing world economy, customer concentration (Apple!), an escalating trade war and a rising dollar.
While the company is front-loading its share based compensation and faces the cost of digesting the CA acquisition, changing its business model will propel operational results even higher in years to come.
The company is also returning massive amounts of cash to shareholders and its dividend yield of over 4% this year is really attractive. We think the Apple related little sell-off offers an opportunity.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, but may initiate a long position in AVGO over the next 72 hours. it (other than from Seeking Alpha).
